definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned word for rented rooms, the fuller form of 'digs'
the workings of a gold field, where prospectors dig

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether their old rented rooms were once a gold-mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from digging: dated slang for lodgings and the excavated site of a mining camp.

definitions.meaning: intruding on someone, as in taking advantage of them
august as an adjective means grand and stately

explanation.surface: A question of whether trespassing happens in the summer month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' with its capital looks like the month, but it is the adjective meaning majestic; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposing on someone is intruding; an imposing figure is grand and stately, like an august one.

clue.text: Charge must be reduced for the spare room

indicators.note: reduced in the sense of broken down into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A host complains that the price must come down for the spare bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' looks like a price cut; it signals that the letters of CHARGE MUST BE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom kept for visitors to stay in is a spare room.

indicators.note: something bizarre is twisted out of its normal shape, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The goddess of love appears with a strange mark on her skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term for a mole or other coloured mark on the skin present from birth.

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring, a well of healing water
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A well-organised bout that never turns nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-run' reads as one adjective, but splits into a spring (SPA) and R for run, a cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's practice bout throws punches without real hostility.

definitions.meaning: to pass something on to another person
a footballer's move from one team to another

explanation.surface: Instructions to pass something on and to switch teams.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both conveying property to someone and a player moving between football teams.

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
I is the Roman numeral for one
p is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: A tin of something going cheap for a single penny.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for something cheap, a real bargain buy.

parts.note: the Beetle is the Volkswagen car; its outer metal casing is meant, not an insect's wing case

explanation.surface: The hard casing of an insect offered as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The insect is a red herring: the Beetle is the VW car, and its shell is the car's outer panels.
explanation.definitionFit: The panelled outer frame of a motor car, such as a VW Beetle's.

clue.text: Usual to win nothing in declamatory style-in bars

parts.note: par is the normal or usual level
to land a prize is to win it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone who normally wins nothing, delivering speeches in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pubs but means bars of music: the musical term for a passage sung in a speaking style.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning sung in a speech-like, recitative manner within measured music.

clue.text: A quiet quarter in church recess

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
SE, south-east, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Finding a calm corner in a church alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular vaulted end of a church, typically behind the altar.

parts.note: bread is slang for money, and breaking up is parting company with an employer, not crumbling a loaf

explanation.surface: Asking which loaf is meant for crumbling into pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money; 'breaking up' is the end of a job, not tearing a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Compensation money given to an employee whose job is ended.

clue.text: Having the full round, of course?

definitions.text: Having the full round, of course?

parts.words: Having the full round, of course?
parts.note: a golf course with a complete round of holes, read as if 'of course' meant 'naturally'

explanation.surface: Someone naturally stays for the whole round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but means a golf course: a full round of golf covers its standard number of holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a golf course with the standard complete number of holes for one round.

clue.text: Once said, incorrectly, to be like bishop's duties

indicators.note: something said incorrectly is wrong in its order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Words once misquoted as a description of a bishop's work.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for a bishop's district, so it describes his pastoral duties.

clue.text: Immature insect's rate of progress under city

indicators.note: in a down answer, the speed piece sits beneath the city piece

parts.note: NY is New York, the city
mph, miles per hour, measures how fast one progresses

explanation.surface: How fast a young bug moves beneath a big town.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The larval stage of insects such as dragonflies, before they are adult.

parts.note: the baritone singer who plays the barber in Rossini's opera, not a close-harmony quartet singer

explanation.surface: A singer of the low-middle part in a barbershop quartet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barber-shop' suggests close-harmony singing, but points to Rossini's opera The Barber of Seville, whose title character is a baritone role.
explanation.definitionFit: The title barber of Rossini's opera, a famous baritone part.

indicators.note: playing about with the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traditional Indian melody being performed in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in Uttar Pradesh that is home to the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Fresh March Wind" from the critic's point of view?

definitions.text: from the critic's point of view?

indicators.note: fresh means made anew, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: air is a wind or breeze

explanation.surface: A critic reviewing a piece titled after a spring breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' signals the anagram, not a breeze. An armchair critic judges from comfort, without hands-on experience.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair critic comments without practical experience, from the comfort of a seat.

definitions.meaning: the epic poet of the Iliad and the Odyssey
a homing pigeon, trained to fly back to its loft

explanation.surface: Asking about the favourite bird of a classical poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The bard of the Iliad, and a racing bird that returns to its loft.

clue.text: Lob, say, and drive at great speed

definitions.meaning: a lob is an example of a ball struck up high
US slang for travelling very fast

explanation.surface: A tennis shot followed by a fast drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A lofted shot is a high ball; American slang for going flat out.

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to tire or strain someone

explanation.surface: A tired person sent on an errand.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax or burden someone, and a piece of assigned work.

clue.text: Room for improvement in waters away from the coast

indicators.note: the room piece goes inside the waters piece

parts.note: seas are large waters
a hospital ward is a room where patients get better

explanation.surface: Things could be better at sea, offshore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room for improvement' sounds like criticism but is a hospital ward, where patients recover.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading out towards the open sea, off the shore.

parts.note: may is the same as might, expressing possibility
to bug is to annoy

explanation.surface: Warning that a certain insect could be annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the cockchafer, a large brown flying insect seen in late spring.

parts.note: a centaur is half beast, half human, so it carries its own rider as one body

explanation.surface: Who rides a mythical half-horse creature?
explanation.walkthrough: A centaur's top half is a man and its lower half a horse, so it is a man on a horse already.
explanation.definitionFit: A centaur combines a mounted rider and his steed in one body.

parts.note: Titian is a bright auburn red, named after the painter's favourite hair colour
a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: A painting by the Venetian master, or a study of his colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colour' is the verb, to blush or turn red; 'Titian' suggests the painter but gives the hair colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To colour up is to blush, flushing crimson.

clue.text: Bart's heir had to move a minute distance

indicators.note: the letters have to move about into a new order

explanation.surface: The heir of a baronet is obliged to relocate a short way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bart' is an abbreviation for baronet; here its letters, with the S, join HEIR and HAD as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny margin, as narrow as the width of one strand of hair.

clue.text: Terrible fellow, seeing Godiva nude in part…

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: A dreadful man spies on Lady Godiva riding naked.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivan the Terrible was a Russian tsar; Lady Godiva rode naked through Coventry in legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan the Terrible was the infamous sixteenth-century tsar.

clue.text: … fellow the church body put up!

indicators.note: in a down answer, put up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: A man whom the congregation has nominated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' looks like nominating but signals reading NAVE upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Welsh male name, standing for any man.

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis
ars is the Latin word for art

explanation.surface: Sharp blades that are fond of ancient sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing implements have flat blades that push the water.

definitions.meaning: the queen who sponsored Columbus, ruling with Ferdinand

explanation.surface: Describing a Spanish monarch as dull.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale greyish-yellow shade; and the Spanish queen who reigned with Ferdinand of Aragon.

definitions.meaning: Edward Lear wrote comic verse full of invented words

explanation.surface: Asking whether a bed belongs to King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear' suggests Shakespeare's king, but it is Edward Lear, the Victorian writer of comic verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear's comic verse is a famous genre of absurd writing; bunk means rubbish talk.
